reason: Nominates one cause: the new email shifts who responds. RCT under fixed routing, within-type satisfaction, and lower reopen rates among old-email respondents separates selection from mix and real service decline.

Nominates only the technical-ticket mix shift. Within-type means plus reweighting to the pre-change 40/60 mix, expecting stability and a result near 4.3, separates composition from within-type quality decline.

Nominates a mobile-specific checkout UI defect. Tag-independent checkout-start-to-paid rates in device-by-channel cells, with mobile down in both channels and desktop flat, separates a checkout regression from mix and measurement.

Single cause is differential response to the new email. Randomization with matched overall reopen rates but higher reopen rates among new-email respondents isolates who answers from an actual service change.

Only respondent selection is nominated. Differential response for reopened versus non-reopened tickets plus higher within-type satisfaction under the old email distinguishes selection from issue mix and broad service decline.

One cause: the new email deters satisfied customers. An invitation RCT with within-type scores and higher reopening among new-email respondents predicts selection rather than routing or ticket-mix change.

Single mix-shift hypothesis. Type-specific before/after means and reweighting to the prior mix, predicting little within-type change and a result near 4.3, checks composition against within-type deterioration.

One cause: mobile checkout friction beyond mix. Processor-joined checkout-start-to-paid rates within paid and non-paid traffic, mobile down and desktop flat, distinguishes regression from channel mix and tag undercount.

One nominated cause: a mobile checkout defect. Device-by-channel conversion and payment-step drop-off with elevated mobile errors, desktop unchanged within channel, separates regression from mix shift.

Single selection mechanism. An invitation RCT under identical routing predicts a 20% versus 10% response gap and higher satisfaction in both issue types, separating email-driven selection from mix and routing.

Primary cause is a mobile payment defect; higher mobile share only amplifies that defect. Within-channel step rates and payment-submit errors, mobile down and desktop flat, tests that regression rather than a second independent cause.

Nominates the technical-share shift alone. Stable within-type means, lower technical scores, and a mix-standardized average near 4.3 are a directional standardization contrast against real within-type worsening.

Nominates a mobile payment block independent of mix. Processor-confirmed payment-page completion by device-by-channel cell plus a mobile error spike, desktop stable, distinguishes UI regression from composition and tracking loss.

Single cause is selective nonresponse to the new email. RCT under current routing predicts about double the response rate, higher within-type satisfaction, and a larger reopened share among new-email respondents.
